analytics.name: Analytic 1567
analytics.guidance: Detects suspicious USB HID device enumeration and keystroke injection patterns, such as rapid sequences of input with no user context, scripts executed through simulated keystrokes, or rogue devices presenting themselves as keyboards.

tuning.description: List of known, legitimate USB vendor/product IDs authorized for use in the enterprise.
Restrict detection to times when no user is logged in or activity is outside business hours.
List of legitimate parent processes expected to spawn PowerShell or scripting engines.

analytics.name: Analytic 1568
analytics.guidance: Detects USB HID device enumeration under `/sys/bus/usb/devices/` and rapid keystroke injection resulting in command execution such as bash or Python scripts launched without interactive user activity.

tuning.description: Track suspicious or unapproved USB vendor/product IDs.
Time threshold for script execution after HID injection, e.g., less than 10 seconds.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve: parent process is usb/hid device handler, child process bash/python invoked

log_sources.name: linux:syslog
log_sources.channel: New HID device enumeration with type 'keyboard' followed by immediate input injection

analytics.name: Analytic 1569
analytics.guidance: Detects abnormal HID device enumeration via I/O Registry (ioreg -p IOUSB) and keystroke injection targeting AppleScript, osascript, or PowerShell equivalents. Defender correlates new USB device connections with rapid script execution.

tuning.description: Whitelist of AppleScripts expected in the environment, to minimize false positives.
Timeframe between HID injection and script execution considered suspicious.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: New IOUSB keyboard/HID device enumerated with suspicious attributes

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: osascript, AppleScript, or Python execution triggered immediately after HID connection
